targets.subject: Pitch for the newsletter on what models get wrong
targets.draft:
Hi,

I'd like to write a practical piece for the MCP newsletter on facts a model gets wrong, and the small server that fixes each one.

The clearest case is the IRS mileage rate. It went from 72.5 to 76 cents on July 1, 2026, after most models were trained, so a model multiplies by the old rate. Live river gauges and 2026 SAT percentiles work the same way.

I run 25 free hosted servers that need no key, and I'd use them only as worked examples. The explainers are at mcpstamp.com/can-claude/. Should I send an outline first?

Michael

not_used.detail: PulseMCP and The Agentic Loop pause all submissions (page last updated September 3, 2026, https://www.pulsemcp.com/submit) and publish no tips address. MCP Bits (Dave Bettin), MCP Weekly Digest and MCPJam publish no tips or contact route on their about pages. MCP Manager's digest offers only a demo booking. Skillselion's MCP Server of the Week gives info@skillselion.com for corrections, citations, press and partnerships, not submissions.

mcp.so shows only an unlabeled footer email icon and a $39 paid tier. mcpservers.org and mcp-archive.com are forms with no contact. MyMCPShelf asks for 10 or more GitHub stars and publishes no address. OpenTools charges an annual subscription. ScriptByAI wants three months of operation and a reciprocal backlink. mcpserverfinder.com lists info@ with no invitation. Glama publishes support@glama.ai for questions, but there is nothing to ask, since 25 of 27 repos have Glama pages today.

No contributing file asks for personal contact. punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers (97,232 stars) takes pull requests only. punkpeye/awesome-remote-mcp-servers says ask in the PR or on Discord. wong2 sends submissions to mcpservers.org. tolkonepiu/best-of-mcp-servers takes an issue or pull request. appcypher, TensorBlock, jaw9c, Sagargupta16 and bhavyshekhaliya route through pull requests. The Remote MCP List repo is dormant (last push 2025-09-05, 152 open issues, remotemcplist.com does not resolve).

No show or channel I fetched publishes a pitch route for MCP tools. ThursdAI lists only host profiles. The Practical AI and AI Engineering Podcast pages returned 404 or moved. The Changelog takes episode requests through a form that needs a sign-in and is not MCP specific. I found no YouTube creator who invites MCP server submissions.

Web Tools Weekly takes tool tips by DM on X or Bluesky, but covers front-end tools and never mentions MCP, so a pitch would be off topic. TLDR, Cooper Press titles, Heavybit DevTools Digest and DevelopersDigest publish no submission route. Agent Commerce Weekly covers x402 payments and invites nothing. Changelog News has a submit form that needs an account and excludes commercial products.

resend_section: Resend can mail people who asked for it, so the safe build is an opt-in signup on mcpstamp.com for an update list (new free servers, new can-claude pages) with the purpose written on the form and a confirmation email. An agent can build the form, the confirm page and the unsubscribe page.

Each signup needs a stored receipt (source, UTC time, purpose, confirmed mailbox) and a working per-person unsubscribe link, because scripts/outreach_send.mjs refuses any row without them and caps a batch at ten.
Resend's acceptable-use policy (read 2026-11-02) bans cold outreach, purchased lists and scraped contact data, and it expects complaints under 0.08 percent and bounces under 4 percent.

zovo.one is the verified sending domain and it also sends license and setup mail, so one cold batch that draws a few complaints would put paying customers' email at risk for a list of strangers who never asked.
So the agents get drafts and a signup page, not a send key for outreach, and the owner sends the packet emails by hand from their own mailbox, one at a time.
If the owner wants agent sending later, create a separate sending_access key limited to the verified domain, keep it in the secret store, and point it only at the opted-in file.
